blocking_issues.description: The bridge lemma quantifier transfer (line 2159) requires showing the depth-k 3-var existential transfers between M and M'. Zone-based witness matching from interval/above/below data finds u' with same depth-(k+1) 1-var NF, but proving the depth-k 3-var NF agrees requires Fraisse-style reasoning: the sub-interval types for configurations with 3+ points cannot be derived from the original 2-point interval data. The Fraisse compression lemma (nf_fraisse_compression, sorry-free) reduces this to proving h_transfer at each depth j < k, but h_transfer itself requires sub-interval matching at recursive levels.

continuation_context.key_mathematical_insight: The game avoids sub-interval matching by using the ORIGINAL interval data at each round. The matched point ends up in (x', t') (not in a sub-interval), but its depth-(k+1) 1-var NF ensures correct behavior. After k rounds, depth-0 atom agreement at (2+k) vars follows from orderings + predicates. The compression lemma then gives depth-k agreement at 2 vars.
